title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 28–30). L is a totally ordered set (possibly with an ideal 'boundary' ∂L of cuts). 'Pseudo-tranches' / 'pseudo-transversales' (ps. tr.) are, in effect, nonempty convex subsets (intervals) of L, degenerate points included. The boundary ∂T of such a T is taken in ∂L. For two of them, T < T' means T lies entirely before T'. They 'se raccordent' (join up) when T ∪ T' is again convex with no gap. T ≪ T' means T < T' and they do not join up. Page 28 proves that in that case there is a unique 'interstitial' tranche S between them, namely S = {x : T < x < T'}.

This page:
- Tr(L) denotes the set of pseudo-tranches of L, ordered by ≪.
- For each finite subset Φ that is totally ordered by ≪, he sets X_Φ = ⋃_{i∈Φ} T_i. This is a disjoint union of pairwise separated intervals.
- Proposition: the map Φ ↦ X_Φ, from Disj*_≪(Tr(L)) (finite ≪-chains, ∅ included) to the power set 𝔓(L), is injective.
- The reason is that the T_i are exactly the maximal convex pieces of X_Φ, because ≪ forbids adjacency. Hence a set of the form X_Φ determines its decomposition.
- Sets of this form are called 'modérées' (tame). They are the finite unions of intervals and points, i.e. the tame subsets of a one-dimensional ordered space.
- He defines a frontier Fr(X_Φ) = (⋃ ∂T_i) \ ε. Here ε removes certain boundary points t: roughly those not occurring as singleton components {t} ∈ Φ, and lying where 𝒰 is a neighbourhood so that {t} is not isolated. The margin calls this a 'relative frontier in L (but not for the topology of L)'.
- The T_i are called the 'connected components' of X (with the caveat 'not for the conical topology'). The set of components is written π_0(X).

Purpose. This builds a purely order-theoretic, one-dimensional 'tame topology': tame sets, their frontier and π_0. Page 30 continues with tame relative position and the tame complement C_mod(X), built from the interstitial tranches. It serves the 'réseaux via découpages' programme, i.e. combinatorial structures obtained by cutting ordered or stratified objects. That programme matches the tame-topology programme announced in the Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: The definition of ε (the frontier points removed) is garbled and partially crossed out. As written it is not clear that Fr(X_Φ) equals the usual topological frontier; Grothendieck himself flags that it is not the frontier for the topology of L.
Injectivity needs ≪ (non-adjacency) rather than mere disjointness. The page's 'Disj*_≪' notation handles this, but the transcription's 'disjoints' alone would make the claim false.

ideas.what: Tame subsets of a totally ordered set are the finite unions of pairwise separated intervals or points. The decomposition into such intervals is unique (injectivity of Φ ↦ X_Φ).
ideas.modern_name: Definable sets in dimension 1 of an o-minimal structure; maximal convex components
ideas.where_published: Programme of 'topologie modérée' only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without this formalism

ideas.what: Frontier of a tame set expressed via endpoints of its components (in a boundary of cuts), minus a correction set ε.
ideas.modern_name: Frontier of definable sets / Dedekind-completion endpoints

ideas.what: Components of a tame set, with set of components π_0(X), defined combinatorially. They are explicitly distinguished from components in a 'conical' topology.

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently develops, in 1986, an axiomatic order-theoretic 'tame' theory of subsets of a line. It covers tame sets, frontier, π_0 and tame relative position. This is contemporaneous with Pillay–Steinhorn's o-minimality, and it is the concrete 1D groundwork of his Esquisse 'topologie modérée' programme, which is otherwise known only from the programmatic sketch.
missed.quote: Les ens de la forme X_Φ s'appellent modérés
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents how Grothendieck actually began formalizing tame topology. This is of historical interest for the o-minimality / tame topology story. Mathematically it is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Mathematically routine one-dimensional material. Historically mildly interesting as a concrete trace of Grothendieck's own 'topologie modérée' foundations in 1986, but nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'adonné par ≪' / 'toute adonnée' should read 'ordonné par ≪' / 'totalement ordonnée'.
'Prop' is a marginal label; the crossed-out heading is 'Définition'.
